reg_deadline.en: Registration closed Monday, October 5, 2026. One exception: if you, or a family member who came with you, left the military or the Merchant Marine, came back from a military deployment, or left a job outside the U.S. after October 5, you can still register in person at your Supervisor of Elections office until 5 p.m. on Friday, October 30. Bring papers that show it.
reg_deadline.es: El registro cerró el lunes 5 de octubre de 2026. Hay una excepción: si tú, o un familiar que vino contigo, dejaste el servicio militar o la Marina Mercante, regresaste de un despliegue militar o dejaste un trabajo fuera de EE. UU. después del 5 de octubre, todavía puedes registrarte en persona en la oficina del supervisor electoral (Supervisor of Elections) hasta las 5 p. m. del viernes 30 de octubre. Lleva documentos que lo demuestren.
reg_deadline.quote: An individual or accompanying family member who has been discharged or separated from the uniformed services or the United States Merchant Marine, has returned from a military deployment or activation, or has separated from employment outside the territorial limits of the United States, after the book-closing date for an election pursuant to s. 97.055 and who is otherwise qualified may register to vote in such election until 5 p.m. on the Friday before that election in the office of the supervisor of elections.
reg_deadline.en_after: Registration closed Monday, October 5, 2026, and the late window for people back from military service or a job abroad closed October 30.
reg_deadline.es_after: El registro cerró el lunes 5 de octubre de 2026, y el plazo tardío para quienes regresaron del servicio militar o de un trabajo en el extranjero cerró el 30 de octubre.
reg_deadline.notes: Oct 5 is from dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/election-dates/ ('Deadline to register to vote: October 5, 2026'). Friday before Nov 3 = Oct 30 (computed).

mail_request.en: Your county Supervisor of Elections must get your request by 5 p.m. on Thursday, October 22, 2026, for a ballot to be mailed to you.
mail_request.es: El Supervisor de Elecciones de tu condado (Supervisor of Elections) debe recibir tu solicitud a más tardar a las 5 p. m. del jueves 22 de octubre de 2026 para que te manden la boleta por correo.
mail_request.quote: Deadline to request that ballot be mailed: October 22, 2026
mail_request.en_after: The deadline to have a ballot mailed to you passed October 22, 2026. You can still vote in person.
mail_request.es_after: La fecha límite para que te manden la boleta por correo pasó el 22 de octubre de 2026. Todavía puedes votar en persona.

mail_return.en: Your Supervisor of Elections must receive it by 7 p.m. local time on Tuesday, November 3. A postmark doesn't count. The Postal Service suggests mailing it at least a week early, or use a secure drop box.
mail_return.es: El Supervisor de Elecciones debe recibirla a más tardar a las 7 p. m., hora local, del martes 3 de noviembre. El matasellos no cuenta. El Servicio Postal recomienda enviarla por lo menos una semana antes, o puedes usar un buzón de entrega seguro.
mail_return.quote: A returned voted ballot must be received, regardless of postmark, by the Supervisor of Elections' office no later than 7:00 pm (local time) on Election Day.

early_hours.en: Every county offers early voting through Saturday, October 31. Some counties add days, as late as Sunday, November 1. Each site is open at least 8 and no more than 12 hours a day. Check your county Supervisor of Elections for exact days and hours.
early_hours.es: Todos los condados ofrecen votación anticipada hasta el sábado 31 de octubre. Algunos condados agregan días, hasta el domingo 1 de noviembre. Cada centro abre por lo menos 8 y no más de 12 horas al día. Consulta al supervisor electoral de tu condado (Supervisor of Elections) para los días y horarios exactos.
early_hours.quote: At a minimum, early voting must be offered starting on the 10 th day before the election and ending on the 3 rd day before the election. Supervisors of Elections may offer more days starting as early as the 15 th day before the election and ending on the 2 nd day before an election. Early voting must hours must be at least 8 hours a day but no more than 12 hours per day at each site during the applicable period.
early_hours.en_after: Early voting is over. On Election Day, vote at your assigned precinct, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
early_hours.es_after: La votación anticipada terminó. El Día de las Elecciones, vota en tu precinto asignado, de 7 a. m. a 7 p. m.
early_hours.notes: 3rd day before Nov 3 = Sat Oct 31; 2nd day before = Sun Nov 1 (computed). election-dates page: 'Early voting period (mandatory period): October 24 – 31, 2026 (Contact Supervisor of Elections for optional days of early voting)'.

cure.notes: The cure deadline is relative (5 p.m. local time on the 2nd day after the election); it is in mail.cure rather than as a computed date here.

in_person.en: During early voting, you can vote at any early voting site in your county. On Election Day, vote at your assigned precinct.
in_person.es: Durante la votación anticipada puedes votar en cualquier centro de votación anticipada de tu condado. El Día de las Elecciones, vota en el precinto que te corresponde.
in_person.quote: Eligible and registered voters can cast a ballot prior to Election Day at any designated early voting site within their county of registration during early voting days and hours.

locator_label.en: Voter Precinct Lookup (Florida Division of Elections)
locator_label.es: Voter Precinct Lookup (División de Elecciones de Florida)

rule.en: Pick your county on the state's Voter Precinct Lookup page to find your Election Day polling place. Moved within your county? You can update your address at your new precinct and vote there. Moved from another Florida county? Some counties let you do the same; elsewhere you vote a provisional ballot, so call your Supervisor of Elections first.
rule.es: Elige tu condado en la página Voter Precinct Lookup del estado para encontrar tu lugar de votación del Día de las Elecciones. ¿Te mudaste dentro de tu condado? Puedes actualizar tu dirección en tu nuevo precinto y votar ahí. ¿Te mudaste desde otro condado de Florida? Algunos condados te dejan hacer lo mismo; en los demás votas con una boleta provisional, así que llama primero al supervisor electoral (Supervisor of Elections).
rule.quote: An elector who moves from the precinct in which the elector is registered may vote in the precinct to which he or she has moved his or her legal residence, if the change of residence is within the same county or the precinct to which the elector has moved his or her legal residence is within a county that uses an electronic database as a precinct register at the polling place, and the elector completes an affirmation
rule.notes: Lookup sentence also on dos.fl.gov election-day-voting page (read 2026-10-21). 101.045(2)(b): a move from outside the county to a county without an electronic precinct register means a provisional ballot. Which counties use e-pollbooks isn't listed, so the copy says 'some counties'.

en: Florida ID card from the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles
Veteran health ID card from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
Florida concealed weapon or firearm license
Employee ID card from the federal government, the state, a county or a city
es: Tarjeta de identificación de Florida del Departamento de Seguridad Vial y Vehículos Motorizados (Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles)
Tarjeta de débito o de crédito
Identificación de un centro de retiro
Identificación de una asociación de vecinos
Tarjeta de salud para veteranos del Departamento de Asuntos de Veteranos de EE. UU.
Licencia de Florida para portar armas ocultas (concealed weapon or firearm license)
Identificación de empleado del gobierno federal, del estado, de un condado o de una ciudad
accepted.quote: Whether voting during early voting or on Election Day, you must bring a current and valid photo ID with signature.

expired.en: Your photo ID must be current and valid. If it doesn't show your signature, bring a second ID that does. Student IDs and debit or credit cards with a photo still count on November 3. A new, shorter ID list starts January 1, 2027.
expired.es: Tu identificación con foto debe estar vigente y ser válida. Si no tiene tu firma, lleva una segunda identificación que la tenga. Las identificaciones de estudiante y las tarjetas de débito o crédito con foto todavía sirven el 3 de noviembre. Una lista nueva y más corta empieza el 1 de enero de 2027.
expired.quote: In 2026, the Florida Legislature revised the list of acceptable forms of IDs in 101.043, Florida Statutes, (ch. 2026-26, Laws of Florida(eff. January 1, 2027) ... If the photo ID does not contain the voter’s signature, the voter can provide another ID that includes the voter’s signature.
expired.notes: DE Reference Guide 0006, Rev. 2026-06-01, read by curl + pdftotext 2026-10-28. The 12-item 2026 list (with student and debit/credit card IDs) is on dos.fl.gov election-day-voting (updated Aug 7, 2026).

without.en: Forgot your ID? You can still vote a provisional ballot. It counts if you're eligible, you voted in the right precinct and the signature on it matches your registration.
without.es: ¿Olvidaste tu identificación? Igual puedes votar con una boleta provisional. Cuenta si puedes votar, votaste en el precinto correcto y la firma coincide con la de tu registro.
without.quote: As long as you are eligible and voted in the proper precinct, your provisional ballot will count provided the signature on your provisional ballot matches the signature in your registration record.

who.en: Any Florida voter can vote by mail. Changed your mind? Bring your mail ballot, marked or not, to your polling place or an early voting site, turn it in and vote a regular ballot. Without it, staff check whether your ballot came in: if not, you vote a regular ballot; if they can't tell, you vote a provisional one. Since early voting began, picking up a mail ballot or having one delivered takes an emergency affidavit (Form DS-DE 162).
who.es: Cualquier votante de Florida puede votar por correo. ¿Cambiaste de opinión? Lleva tu boleta por correo, marcada o no, a tu lugar de votación o a un centro de votación anticipada, entrégala y vota con una boleta regular. Si no la llevas, el personal revisa si tu boleta ya llegó: si no llegó, votas con una boleta regular; si no lo pueden saber, votas con una provisional. Desde que empezó la votación anticipada, recoger una boleta por correo o pedir que te la entreguen requiere una declaración jurada de emergencia (formulario DS-DE 162).
who.quote: The voter should bring the ballot (marked or unmarked) to the polls to turn the ballot in and vote a regular ballot. If the voter does not bring the ballot to the polls for whatever reason, the Supervisor of Elections' office will need to confirm that the ballot has not already been returned and received. If the ballot has not been received, the voter will be allowed to vote a regular ballot. If it cannot be determined if the ballot has been received, the voter will be allowed to vote a provisional ballot. ... If a voter or designee waits until the start of mandatory early voting or up through Election Day to pick up or have delivered a vote-by-mail ballot, a special affidavit must also be completed.
who.notes: 'Any Florida voter can vote by mail' was read on dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/voting/ (2026-10-21). If the ballot was already received, the voter is deemed to have voted (101.69(1)(a)); a voter who disagrees gets a provisional ballot.

witness.en: Sign the voter's certificate on the return envelope. Your county matches it against the signature on your voter record, so update your signature if it has changed.
witness.es: Firma el certificado del votante en el sobre de devolución. Tu condado lo compara con la firma de tu registro de votante, así que actualiza tu firma si ha cambiado.
witness.quote: The signatures must match in order for the ballot or petition to count or other change to be made.

cure.en: Signature missing or doesn't match? Your Supervisor of Elections will let you know. Send back a Vote-by-Mail Ballot Cure Affidavit with a copy of your ID by 5 p.m. local time on Thursday, November 5, the second day after the election. You can return it by mail, email, fax or in person.
cure.es: ¿Falta tu firma o no coincide? El supervisor electoral (Supervisor of Elections) te avisará. Devuelve la declaración jurada para corregir tu boleta por correo (Vote-by-Mail Ballot Cure Affidavit) con una copia de tu identificación a más tardar a las 5 p. m., hora local, del jueves 5 de noviembre, el segundo día después de la elección. Puedes devolverla por correo, email, fax o en persona.
cure.quote: The form and copy of the ID can be returned by mail, email, fax, or in person. The deadline to submit the form and the ID is no later than 5 p.m. (local time) on the 2nd day after an election.
cure.en_after: The deadline to fix a mail ballot signature was 5 p.m. local time on Thursday, November 5, 2026.
cure.es_after: La fecha límite para corregir la firma de una boleta por correo fue a las 5 p. m., hora local, del jueves 5 de noviembre de 2026.
cure.notes: Second day after Nov 3 = Thu Nov 5 (computed).

dropbox.en: Secure drop boxes are at your Supervisor of Elections' main and branch offices until 7 p.m. local time on Election Day, and at early voting sites. Your county's website lists the locations, days and hours.
dropbox.es: Hay buzones de entrega seguros en la oficina principal y las sucursales del Supervisor de Elecciones hasta las 7 p. m., hora local, del Día de las Elecciones, y en los centros de votación anticipada. El sitio web de tu condado tiene los lugares, días y horarios.
dropbox.quote: Vote-by-mail ballots may also be deposited into secure drop boxes at Supervisors of Elections' main and branch offices until 7:00 pm (local time) on Election Day.

gear.en: Campaigning stops 150 feet from the entrance to a polling place, early voting site or drop box. In that zone, no one can ask for votes, hand out campaign material or petitions, or try to influence voters.
gear.es: La campaña se detiene a 150 pies de la entrada de un lugar de votación, de un centro de votación anticipada o de un buzón de entrega. En esa zona nadie puede pedir votos, repartir material de campaña o peticiones, ni tratar de influir en los votantes.
gear.quote: No person, political committee, or other group or organization may solicit voters inside the polling place or within 150 feet of a secure ballot intake station or the entrance to any polling place,

phone.en: Take your sticker selfie outside. In the polling room or early voting area, the only photo you can take is of your own ballot.
phone.es: Tómate la selfie con tu sticker afuera. En la sala de votación o el área de votación anticipada, la única foto que puedes tomar es la de tu propia boleta.
phone.quote: No photography is permitted in the polling room or early voting area, except an elector may photograph his or her own ballot.

line.en: If you're in line when the polls close, stay in line. You can still vote.
line.es: Si estás en la fila cuando cierran las casillas, no te salgas. Todavía puedes votar.
line.quote: Any elector who is in line at the time of the official closing of the polls shall be allowed to cast a vote in the election.

tradition.en: Some Florida counties pick their stickers in student contests. In Sarasota County, a seventh grader's pink flamingo, chosen from more than 175 student entries, is the sticker for November 3, offered to everyone who votes by mail, early or on Election Day.
tradition.es: Algunos condados de Florida eligen sus stickers en concursos para estudiantes. En el condado de Sarasota, un flamenco rosa dibujado por un estudiante de séptimo grado, elegido entre más de 175 propuestas, es el sticker del 3 de noviembre, y se le ofrece a todo el que vote por correo, por anticipado o el Día de las Elecciones.
tradition.quote: This year, a pink flamingo is at the center of the sticker, and I think the voters are going to love this design as much as they did the previous one.

early.en: In Clay County, yes. The winning design from the county's student sticker contest is handed out during early voting and on Election Day in 2026.
early.es: En el condado de Clay, sí. El diseño ganador del concurso de stickers del condado se entrega durante la votación anticipada y el Día de las Elecciones en 2026.
early.quote: One original sticker design will be chosen and reproduced for distribution during Early Voting and Election Day for both the Primary and General Elections in 2026.

mail.en: In Sarasota County, yes. The Supervisor of Elections says anyone who votes by mail will be offered the county's 2026 "I Voted" sticker, the pink flamingo design. Ask the Supervisor of Elections office how to get yours.
mail.es: En el condado de Sarasota, sí. El Supervisor de Elecciones (Supervisor of Elections) dice que a todo el que vote por correo se le ofrecerá el sticker de "I Voted" de 2026 del condado, el del flamenco rosa. Pregunta en la oficina del Supervisor de Elecciones cómo conseguir el tuyo.
mail.quote: Anyone who votes by mail (absentee), early in-person or on election day will be offered an “I Voted” sticker.
mail.notes: Release posted April 9, 2026, read in Chrome (WebFetch gets a 403). It does not say how mail voters receive the sticker (packet, office or drop-off). Vote-by-Mail team number 941.861.8618 is from the same site's Notice of Elections and driver license posts. Checked Oct 28 with no official mail-sticker statement found: Orange (voteorangefl.gov; an undated older page said stickers went in vote-by-mail packets but it now 404s and the site search shows nothing current), Pinellas (votepinellas.gov/IVoted digital sticker page now 404s), Hillsborough (2026 contest sticker 'given to voters', no mail mention), Palm Beach (2026 contest stickers for polling locations), Miami-Dade and Broward (nothing found).

provisional.en: You vote a provisional ballot if your eligibility is challenged at the polls or you don't have ID. You have until 5 p.m. local time on the second day after the election to show more proof that you're eligible. It counts if your signature matches your registration and you're eligible.
provisional.es: Votas con una boleta provisional si cuestionan en el lugar de votación si puedes votar o si no tienes identificación. Tienes hasta las 5 p. m., hora local, del segundo día después de la elección para mostrar más pruebas de que puedes votar. Cuenta si tu firma coincide con la de tu registro y puedes votar.
provisional.quote: You have up until 5 PM (local time) on the second day after the election to present further evidence of your eligibility in order for your ballot to count.

line.en: You can still vote. Anyone waiting in line when the polls close on Election Day gets to cast a ballot.
line.es: Igual puedes votar. Toda persona que esté en la fila cuando cierran las casillas el Día de las Elecciones puede votar.
line.quote: Any elector who is in line at the time of the official closing of the polls shall be allowed to cast a vote in the election.
line.notes: Was '7 p.m. local time', which misleads Gulf County voters on Central time (polls close 6 p.m. CT).

track.en: Find your county's link on the state's Vote-by-Mail Ballot Information and Status Lookup page and check your ballot there.
track.es: Busca el enlace de tu condado en la página Vote-by-Mail Ballot Information and Status Lookup del estado y revisa ahí tu boleta.
track.quote: To track online your vote-by-mail ballot, visit our webpage for county-specific links at Vote-by-Mail Ballot Information and Status Lookup.

notes: Read October 21, 2026 on dos.fl.gov (curl worked), flsenate.gov and sarasotavotes.gov (Chrome; WebFetch got 403). Early voting dates in states.js (Oct. 24 to 31) match dos.fl.gov/elections/for-voters/election-dates/: 'Early voting period (mandatory period): October 24 – 31, 2026'. ID CONFLICT, resolved: the 2026 Florida Statutes on flsenate.gov (s. 101.043, amended by ch. 2026-26) list seven IDs and drop debit/credit cards, student IDs, retirement center, neighborhood association and public assistance IDs, but the Division of Elections' 'Florida History of Voter Identification Requirements' guide (DE Reference Guide 0006, updated 06/2026, soe.dos.state.fl.us) says that list is 'eff. January 1, 2027'. The 12-item list on dos.fl.gov's Election Day Voting page (updated August 7, 2026) is the one for November 3, 2026, and is used here. Re-check before any 2027 election; the student ID change is also in federal litigation (complaint filed October 16, 2026, read only in search results). The 2026 statute page is cited only for 102.031 (no-solicitation zone and photography), which ch. 2026-26 did not touch (last amended 2022). Mail return, cure and provisional deadlines are relative to the election on the official pages; no calendar dates computed. Clothing: 102.031 bans solicitation within 150 feet but no official page says whether campaign clothing counts, so the gear fact doesn't mention clothing. No statewide sticker found; the sticker fact is Sarasota County only.

hours.en: Polling places are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., on the time used in your county seat. In Gulf County, that's Eastern time, so polls in the county's Central time area open at 6 a.m. and close at 6 p.m. Central.
hours.es: Los lugares de votación abren de 7 a. m. a 7 p. m., según la hora que se usa en la cabecera de tu condado. En el condado de Gulf es la hora del Este, así que en la parte del condado con hora del Centro abren a las 6 a. m. y cierran a las 6 p. m., hora del Centro.
hours.quote: The polls shall be open at the voting places at 7:00 a.m., on the day of the election, and shall be kept open until 7:00 p.m., of the same day, and the time shall be regulated by the customary time in standard use in the county seat of the locality.
hours.notes: Gulf County Supervisor of Elections, votegulf.gov/voters/vote-on-election-day/ (read 2026-10-28): 'Polls open at 7:00 AM (ET), 6:00 AM (CT) Polls close at 7:00 PM (ET), 6:00 PM (CT)'. Gulf is the county split between time zones (Perplexity lead; split not checked against an official map).
